name: Washington, D.C.
operatingHours: Metrorail runs 5:00 AM–midnight Mon–Thu, 5:00 AM–2:00 AM Fri, 6:00 AM–2:00 AM Sat and 6:00 AM–midnight Sun. First and last trains vary by station; there is no all-night rail service.
fareInfo: Fares depend on distance: $2.25–$6.75 per ride at weekday daytime, with a flat fare of $2.25–$2.50 on weekends and late weekday evenings (2026). Tap a contactless bank card or phone at the faregate, or use a SmarTrip card (also in Apple/Google Wallet). Unlimited passes cost $13.50 for 1 day and $33.75 for 3 days. Metro–bus transfers within 2 hours are discounted.

lines.name: Blue Line
lines.firstLast: Reagan National Airport station: first ~5:00 AM (7 AM Sat/Sun), last ~midnight (1 AM Fri–Sat); ~15 min to downtown.

lines.name: Silver Line
lines.firstLast: Dulles Airport station: first ~5:00 AM (7 AM Sat/Sun), last ~midnight (1 AM Fri–Sat); ~50 min to Metro Center. Peak/off-peak fares up to $6.75.

lines.name: Yellow Line
lines.firstLast: Reagan National Airport station: first ~5:00 AM (7 AM Sat/Sun), last ~midnight (1 AM Fri–Sat); ~15 min to downtown.

sights.name: National Air and Space Museum
sights.note: The Smithsonian's flagship of flight, from the Wright Flyer and Spirit of St. Louis to Apollo 11's command module; the building is mid-renovation, with the last galleries due to reopen in late 2026.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:30 PM daily (last entry 5:15 PM); free timed-entry pass required

sights.name: Lincoln Memorial
sights.note: The marble temple with the seated Lincoln at the west end of the Mall, overlooking the Reflecting Pool; especially atmospheric after dark.
sights.hours: Open 24 hours; rangers on site ~9:30 AM–10:00 PM

sights.name: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History
sights.note: Dinosaur hall, the Hope Diamond and a huge African elephant in the rotunda; free and one of the busiest museums in the world.

sights.name: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum
sights.note: A sober, powerful chronological exhibition on the Holocaust built around survivors' artifacts and testimony; recommended for ages 11 and up.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:30 PM daily; free timed pass needed for the Permanent Exhibition

sights.name: National Gallery of Art
sights.note: Free national art collection in two buildings linked by a light tunnel: old masters (the only Leonardo in the Americas) in the West Building, modern art in the East.

sights.name: Library of Congress
sights.note: The Thomas Jefferson Building's gilded Great Hall and Main Reading Room overlook, plus Jefferson's reconstructed library; linked to the Capitol by tunnel.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:00 PM Tue, Wed, Fri & Sat; till 8:00 PM Thu; closed Sun & Mon; free timed-entry ticket required

sights.name: Washington Monument
sights.note: The 555-ft marble obelisk at the heart of the Mall; an elevator runs to a 500-ft observation level with views in every direction.
sights.hours: 9:00 AM–5:00 PM daily (closed one day a month for maintenance); timed tickets via Recreation.gov, a few same-day passes at 8:45 AM

sights.name: The National Mall
sights.note: Two miles of lawn and paths from the Capitol to the Lincoln Memorial, lined with free Smithsonian museums and the major memorials.

sights.name: International Spy Museum
sights.note: A hands-on museum of espionage gadgets, real cases and spy tradecraft, where you take on a cover identity as you go.
sights.hours: ~10:00 AM–6:00 PM daily (later on some weekends)

sights.name: U.S. Capitol
sights.note: Seat of Congress under its cast-iron dome; free guided tours of the Rotunda and Crypt start at the underground Visitor Center on the east side.
sights.hours: Visitor Center 8:30 AM–4:30 PM Mon–Sat; closed Sun

sights.name: National Museum of African American History and Culture
sights.note: The bronze-latticed Smithsonian museum tracing African American history from slavery through civil rights to music, sport and culture; plan several hours.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–5:30 PM Tue–Sun, noon–5:30 PM Mon (last entry 4:00 PM); free timed-entry pass required

sights.name: Ford's Theatre
sights.note: The working theatre where Lincoln was shot in 1865, with a museum below and the Petersen House, where he died, across the street.
sights.hours: Usually ~9:00 AM–4:30 PM; schedule varies around performances; timed tickets every half hour

sights.name: Museum Of The Bible
sights.note: Six floors on the Bible's history and influence, with ancient manuscripts, immersive galleries and a rooftop garden view; free on Tuesdays.

sights.name: United States Botanic Garden
sights.note: A free glasshouse conservatory at the foot of the Capitol with a jungle room, orchids and desert plants, plus an outdoor garden.

sights.name: Washington National Cathedral
sights.note: A Gothic cathedral built over 83 years, with soaring stained glass, a Darth Vader gargoyle and city views from its hilltop; tower restoration has closed some garden areas.
sights.hours: Sightseeing ~10:00 AM–5:00 PM Mon–Fri, to ~4:00 PM Sat, limited Sun; paid sightseeing ticket

sights.name: Vietnam Veterans Memorial
sights.note: Maya Lin's black granite wall engraved with more than 58,000 names, cut into the ground near the Lincoln Memorial.

sights.name: Eastern Market
sights.note: Capitol Hill's 1873 brick market hall with butchers, bakers and a crab-cake counter inside, plus a weekend flea and craft market outside.
sights.hours: 7:00 AM–7:00 PM Tue–Fri, 7:00 AM–6:00 PM Sat, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM Sun; closed Mon

sights.name: Georgetown Waterfront Park
sights.note: A free riverside park on the Potomac at the foot of Georgetown, with fountains, river views toward the Kennedy Center and waterfront bars nearby.

railStations.name: Washington Union Station
railStations.note: Amtrak hub: Acela and Northeast Regional to Philadelphia, New York (~2h45m–3h30m) and Boston; long-distance trains to Chicago, Florida and New Orleans; MARC and VRE commuter rail. Metro Red Line in the station.
railStations.hours: Station concourse open ~5:00 AM–midnight; Amtrak trains run to individual timetables.

airports.name: Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport
airports.transitNote: Metro Blue and Yellow lines (on this map) stop at the airport station, linked to the terminals by walkway; ~15–20 min to L'Enfant Plaza or Gallery Place, ~$2.25–$2.75.
airports.hours: Metro: first train ~5:00 AM weekdays (~6:00 AM weekends), last ~midnight (~2:00 AM Fri & Sat nights).

airports.name: Washington Dulles International Airport
airports.transitNote: Metro Silver Line (on this map) from the Dulles Airport station, a ~5–10 min walk via tunnel from the main terminal; ~50 min to Metro Center, ~$6 at weekday peak.
airports.hours: Silver Line: first train ~5:00 AM weekdays (~6:00 AM weekends), last ~11:30 PM (~1:30 AM Fri & Sat nights).
